Can you use the proper literal here to denote if this ms/s?
We use that form request that gets sent to the device and as per the spec that field does not have a concrete unit. Added comment for better readability.
Same comments as TLIMIT sensor to avoid code dup.

GetTemperature and GetPower are two distinct command with entirely separate request and response fields. We can make an abstract class for all numeric sensor types (temperature, power, voltage, energy, etc) but since they all have distinct request and response fields, such abstract would save some (not substantial though) code duplication but at the cost of additional infrastructure and loss in readability.

You would be passing the encode/decode as std::functions, so I don't know if there would be code duplication (definitely less than what we have now) or loss of readability. I'm fine to hold on this rework until you hear from other revewers/maintainers either way.

I commented this somewhere else, but comments like this aren't useful.

1. The variable is instanceId, not instance_id.
2. I'm pretty sure I can figure out that instanceId means instance id without this comment.

Please just remove the doxygen comments as there's no requirement for full doxygen.  Please leave comments in prose where there are subtleties about how the API is used.
Removed.

Not sure where this was introduced, but there's no need for an abstract class here for every sensor.  We know all the sensor types at compile time, and there's a finite number of them.  Just enumerate them in the main GPU device class.

@ed@tanous.net is your concern with the abstract GpuSensor class or introducing the new GpuPowerSensor class or both?

I also think (I have an old unresolved commit on this patch) that we likely need just one class for the sensor (is this what you are also suggesting)? There are some subtle differences b/w the sensor types - the request message for eg, but those can just be arguments to the main sensor class constructor or just be called according to the sensor type/ID.
Don't think we need this, as commented elsewhere.
Removed.
Do we need a sanity check on the power value before division?
Not needed since a double can hold all value of uint32_t.
Is there a reason these need to be shared_ptrs ?
Yes. The Sensor class doesn't have a default constructor and we need to create them after construction of the `GpuDevice` class.
please don't use auto in contexts where the result isn't duplicated.  Please fix everywhere.
